title: Starting Small, Starting Green

body.en: Kwame started with one skill — repairing small electronics — and one observation: broken solar lanterns in his neighbourhood were being thrown away instead of fixed, even though most just needed a battery replacement. He began collecting them, fixing what he could, and reselling working units at half the price of new ones. No investor, no loan, just a repair skill and a gap nobody else had noticed. A year in, he's training two younger guys from his area to do the same thing. The green economy doesn't always start with a business plan. Sometimes it starts with noticing what everyone else is throwing away.

followUpQuestion: What gap did Kwame notice that turned into a small business?
